decisions_needed.topic: Seed mark after a password rehash (auth R2-29 meets site R2-2)
decisions_needed.context: User #1 is the admin account that exists from the start. While the switch is off, the start-up copies the admin's password from the setting EDGE_PASSWORD_VERIFIER into the account, but only while the account still holds the copy the start-up itself wrote. It tells by a fingerprint of that copy (identities.seed_verifier_sha256, site track). Separately, the auth track replaces an old-format password hash with a new one at the next switch-on sign-in; the password stays the same. After that replacement the stored hash no longer matches the fingerprint, so every later beta start treats the account as having set its own password and stops copying from EDGE_PASSWORD_VERIFIER. If the admin later changes EDGE_PASSWORD_VERIFIER on the beta, the live site keeps the old password. No test covers this case, and it only matters once the switch is on (the live site).
decisions_needed.options: A: keep as merged (after the first switch-on sign-in, the account counts as having its own password; changing the admin password then means a change or reset on live). B: when the rehash replaces a hash that is still the start-up's copy, update the fingerprint too, so later changes to EDGE_PASSWORD_VERIFIER keep reaching the account; the start-up would then write the old-format hash back and the next sign-in would rehash it again.
decisions_needed.recommendation: A, since it is safe and matches the R2-2 rule ('never overwritten once the identity differs from the seed's copy'); record it in CONTRACT 1 next to the seed mark.

done: 1. Email retention of 30 days (Decisions from the fix round, item 2, 'a'). I changed migration 20261119_012 in place; it is unapplied, and its two indexes and its EXECUTE grant are kept. purge_email_outbox now also deletes every sent, failed, expired or suppressed row of every address once it is 30 days old. The 24 h rule for addresses with no account stays. Pending and sending rows are never deleted. A new function, purge_email_hook_events, deletes webhook deliveries after 30 days; it is SECURITY DEFINER with a fixed search_path and only edge_bff_runtime may execute it. A new accounts.purge_codes deletes email codes 30 days after they were used, or after they expired unused; a live code is never deleted. store.PURGES gains 'codes' and 'hook_events', and store.ready() checks for the new function. email_suppression is never purged. edge_bff_runtime still holds no DELETE on the outbox or on the webhook deliveries. Tests run as a login with only the runtime grants, with rows aged 29 and 31 days on each side of each rule.

2. A new authenticator now needs an MFA pass within the last 10 minutes. FlowStore.enroll checks the request session's mfa_passed_at under the enrolment's row lock, using the database clock. An older pass, or none, gets 403 MFA_REQUIRED with details {mfa_enrolled: true, recent_s: 600}, and errors.words gives it its own sentence. After that refusal, the /mfa page in edge-app.js takes a fresh code and then starts the set-up again by itself. The first enrolment is unchanged. The re-check's own test (test_cp1a_f3: re-enrol right after a verify) and test_fix_auth's re-enrolment test pass unchanged. A Chromium test covers the page.

3. public_data on the Terminal relay (ERRORS M260, 'a'). terminal_access.relayed now returns a pair (refusal, data). For a 2xx answer, the data has passed through client.public_data. A cut's bytes and a logo are still relayed unparsed. Callers: main.py forward_terminal and relay_cut, and pages.py index. The file grant keeps the raw answer, because only edge-bff reads its presigned URL. I first checked that no page module or forwarded terminal-api route reads a PRIVATE_KEYS field. A file keyed by ticker whose other columns hold only text or null is sent whole. 2. Guest principal. apps/edge-bff/app/principal.py guest_principal reads the guest plan on every guest request, through the same read_grants, can() and version code as every plan. Guests are switched by EDGE_GUESTS: on by default on the live site, off on the beta, and refused at start when EDGE_MULTIUSER is off.

2. Client address. client_of reads the right-most X-Forwarded-For entry (the hop Railway's edge adds) and uses it only if it parses as an IP address. With no readable address there is no guest principal and the answer is 401 (fail closed). The socket peer is used only when EDGE_ENVIRONMENT=local.

2. Per-visitor quotas. edge-bff sends x-terminal-client, a 32-hex HMAC of the address (never the address itself). terminal-api then counts usage, the quota lock, frees_in and audit rows per visitor under the one guest owner 'edge-guest'. Without the header the owner's row is counted as a whole, which is stricter. Migration database/migrations/20261119_170_terminal_access_log_client.sql (not applied) adds client_key and the partial index access_log_client_at. Measured locally: 151 ms / 300,665 buffers without the index, 0.26 ms / 107 buffers with it.

The search lists every ticker and marks the ones the plan lacks; a remembered ticker the plan does not hold never locks the page. A locked ticker, a locked indicator, or layouts without terminal.layouts makes the Terminal ask the shell for a box (app/locked.ts). The shell's LockedDialog shows sign in / create account to a guest, and to an account the upgrade box with 'Coming soon' plus EDGE_UPGRADE_CONTACT (or that the contact comes soon). Wording is in static/edge-labels.js EdgeLabels.locked. Registration, its verify step and register-code resends answer 403 REGISTRATION_CLOSED, and the register page says registration opens soon. Only the admin (by catalog: '*' or admin.access) and accounts with users.test_account can sign in; everyone else gets 403 SIGN_IN_CLOSED. The test_account mark only changes together with its admin_audit row in the same transaction (deferred trigger). scripts/edge_test_account.py and scripts/onboarding/edge_test_account_job.py create or mark a test account for an address and a plan; they print only user id, username, plan and outcome. decisions_needed.topic: Client-address probe before guests go live
decisions_needed.context: Visitors' Terminal quotas are counted per client address. The address is taken from the right-most X-Forwarded-For entry that Railway's edge adds. The Phase 0 probe that would prove what Railway really sends has not run. If Railway gave every visitor the same address, all visitors would share one quota (stricter, never looser).
decisions_needed.options: (a) run the probe (a Railway call, with the user's go) before the live site opens to visitors; (b) open guests without it

decisions_needed.topic: A ceiling for all visitors together
decisions_needed.context: Quotas per address do not limit a visitor who changes address. Each visitor gets terminal-api's default quotas: 60 files and 30 tickers per hour, 150 tickers and 300 MB per day. The guest plan has no quota rows of its own.
decisions_needed.options: (a) no total ceiling for now; (b) add a total per hour for the guest owner as a new terminal-api quota (data)

decisions_needed.topic: Probe the visitor's address on Railway before guests open on the live site
decisions_needed.context: The live website will let a visitor without an account open the Terminal, using the 'guest' plan (today BBCA's chart). Each visitor's download limits are counted from their address, which edge-bff reads from the last hop of Railway's X-Forwarded-For header. The check that proves what Railway's edge actually sends (CONTRACT section 4, 'Client IP') has never run. If Railway sent one address for everyone, every visitor would share one quota: stricter, never looser.
decisions_needed.options: (a) Run the probe before the live site opens to visitors. It is one Railway call and needs your go. (b) Open guests without it and accept the shared-quota worst case.
decisions_needed.recommendation: (a). The same probe also unblocks the per-address sign-in limit (SIGNIN_IP, R2-37).

decisions_needed.topic: A ceiling for all visitors together
decisions_needed.context: Today each visitor gets terminal-api's default quotas per address: 60 files and 30 tickers an hour, 150 tickers and 300 MB a day. A visitor who keeps changing address is not bounded by that. The guest plan has no quota row of its own.
decisions_needed.options: (a) No overall ceiling for now. (b) A total per hour for the guest owner, set as data (a new terminal-api quota).
decisions_needed.recommendation: (b) before launch: it is a data row and bounds the cost no matter how many addresses are used.

decisions_needed.topic: Bonds and logos in the search for the free plan and guests
decisions_needed.context: Since decision 1 the free plan and guests see the whole ticker list, with locks. The bond list stays filtered because its columns carry dataset dates, so bonds do not appear in their search. Logos stay filtered because edge-bff refuses another ticker's logo image, so locked tickers show a monogram.
decisions_needed.options: (a) Keep as is. (b) Treat the bond list as names only, so bonds appear in the search with a lock, and/or open logo images to every plan.
decisions_needed.recommendation: (a) until the live site is tried; it is the fail-closed reading.

decisions_needed.topic: Readings the tracks took on the live site, for the main agent to confirm with the user
